summary: KAITLYNN HAS CHURNED. On 2026-09-08 at 14:21 she wrote "I need the final invoice and an alternative way to make payments immediately since I cannot wire :) thank you". Stephski issued the closing invoice ten hours later — "here is your final invoice with us, can you please shoot over the remaining balance so we can close out your account with us ❤️" (2026-09-09) — she paid in full on 2026-09-10 ("Paid !! Thank you so much for everything 🙏🏼") and left the chat two minutes later. Nobody at ALTR asked her why, asked her to stay, or acknowledged that a five-week-old client had just terminated. Derrek was in the chat on 2026-09-09 and spoke only about the payment rail. This report covers the full two weeks 2026-08-28 → 2026-09-11, which includes the previously-unpublished 2026-09-04 findings. The first half looked like a recovery: she re-engaged at record volume, Ollie delivered the first performance report ever written on this account (2026-08-29), Mica converted a 20-day-cold Calendly in six minutes (2026-08-31), Stephski restarted invoicing after a 17-day blackout (2026-09-01), and Mayson booked a 21-day-overdue call in 34 seconds (2026-09-04). The second half is the bill for everything that was never done. In the 96 hours after the call was agreed, ALTR answered none of her open items: the free-nude-preview policy breach she raised with a screenshot on 2026-09-04 got "Will look into this now" from Ollie and then silence for 7 days; the $91.00 Derrek waived as a "coupon" was never corrected and she has now paid it; the Google Drive that blocks hundreds of her videos was never confirmed fixed; she was never told which Instagram account she was making 30 reels a month for. On 2026-09-07 Ollie asked "Hey @kaitlynnandersonof have you changed your password?" — she had locked ALTR out of her OnlyFans account, the loudest possible churn signal, and nobody escalated it. She gave notice 24 hours later. The proximate trigger was billing: her wire was rejected on 2026-09-08, the exact due date of the Aug 15-31 invoice, over a payment-path problem she first reported on 2026-08-21 and which was never diagnosed in 19 days. When she finally demanded an alternative, Derrek approved it in two minutes and Stephski produced a working payment link in 37 minutes. That rail existed the whole time and was never offered.

Between 2026-09-04 09:15 and 2026-09-08 14:21 — 101 hours — ALTR posted exactly two messages to this client, one of which was a question asking why she had changed her password. Every single carried-over item on this account closed unresolved: the Aug 19 never-sold drop at 35 days and six consecutive reports, the 'I'm back' voice memo at 35 days, her wall-post cadence request at 28 days, her invoicing-cadence question at 25 days, the wire friction at 21 days, the $91 waiver reversal at 21 days, the revenue-drop complaint at 14 days, the Instagram flagging disclosures at 14 days, the freeloader screenshots at 13 days, the Instagram account name at 12 days, the Drive failure at 9 days, and the nude-preview breach at 7 days.
